name: Marc Carr
life: “I still remember finding my name thanked by a family I barely remembered helping.” Monday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Marc can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I am the neighbor named in three different cards. I asked if the station could help me move my sofa next month.
appearance: Marc is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a little coil of soft measuring tape, Marc looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Marc treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To collect the promised help moving the sofa.
family: Frankie Levin is Marc’s half-sibling. Marc chooses the music. Frankie puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The release address*, Frankie says, “I used to bring him drugs. He asked me for the number of a furniture mover and nothing else.”
connections: Luz Dean (neighbor). A watch worker thanks the person who knows which child's school bag stays behind the orange boxes.

reactions.situation: A colleague leaves a name off the thank-you wall
reactions.response: Marc allows a private thank-you to stay private even on unveiling day.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Marc asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.

reactions.situation: If a frightened person needs longer
reactions.response: Marc changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
